findings.title: The Punk's art cache dies with the warm-up's throwaway rig: every wave's first Punk re-reads punk.glb on its spawn frame
findings.detail:
**What happens.**
- RoomKit.warm_up_art() loads punk_art.tres into a throwaway HumanoidRig, builds it and queue_free()s it.
- SkinnedArt's cache Entry holds its CharacterArt only by WeakRef.
- EnemyCatalog.scene() and EncounterSpawner load street_punk.tscn afresh on each spawn and hold nothing.
- So once the throwaway rig is freed, at the end of the room's first frame, the CharacterArt is freed. The first wave spawns 3 s later (wave_gap_s), loads a new CharacterArt, misses the cache, and runs SkinnedArt._read() on the spawn frame: GLB instantiate, the per-vertex weight and CUSTOM0/1 loops, and a new ArrayMesh to upload.
- The same happens to the first Punk of every later wave once the previous wave's Punks have vanished.

**Cost and why the hero is spared.** Measured headless on this loaded machine: 19.2 ms for the first Punk after the warm-up, 18.7 ms after the street empties, 2.2 ms for a Punk spawned while another lives. A cold read alone is 19.1 ms (punk.glb) and 25.0 ms (player.glb). The hero is spared only because PlayerCharacter.worn_art() holds his art in a static dictionary.

**Why it matters.** A16's soft bars are a spawn hitch at most 33 ms and a first-spawn hitch at most main + 2 ms. SL-int's vsync-on figures already miss the 33 ms bar (spawn hitch 38.3 ms). The warm-up exists to keep that frame clean. In first person this reads as a stutter as each wave's first Punk walks in.

**What the warm-up still does.** Its pipeline purpose still works: the new ArrayMesh has the same vertex format, so nothing compiles.

- game/actors/skinned_art.gd:41 and :193-203 (art_ref: WeakRef; dead entries erased, then a new _read)

findings.title: A7's strain ratchet cannot fail: problems_max is above the most problem lines a run can produce, and the extremes are unratcheted
findings.detail:
**Why the cap is unreachable.** ArtStrain.problems_of() gives each sample at most two strain-range lines (p99.9/p0.1 and max/min), plus a floor line and a NaN line, which are asserted to be 0 separately. Each of the 6 peak flexes can add one triangle line. So a run can have at most:
- Punk: 251 x 2 + 6 = 508 lines, against problems_max 560;
- hero: 236 x 2 + 6 = 478 lines, against problems_max 480.

Today the Punk has 503 and the hero 472: every sample already carries both lines except one (in_bar is 1 on each). No strain regression in any clip can raise the count past the cap.

**What actually guards A7.** Only two numbers:
- the single worst p99.9 (4.6 against 4.12; 9.5 against 8.67);
- one shared flex share of 2% (against 1.62% and 0.63%; for the hero that is a 3x margin).

**What is not held at all.** p0.1, the max and min edge, and every sample other than the worst. A mis-weighted vertex that took the Punk's worst compression from x0.02 to x0.001, or the hero's x37 stretch to x200, passes test_skinned_art and done-when A7 alike.
findings.evidence:
**Code:**
- tests/art_strain.gd:36-40 (SHIPPED problems_max 560 and 480, FLEX_RATCHET_SHARE 0.02)

- assertions at tests/test_m4_done_when.gd:559 and tests/test_skinned_art.gd:1585

**Today's figures:** DONE-WHEN A7 'punk: 251 samples, 1 with every number inside the bars, worst p99.9 4.12, 503 problem lines {strain range 500, triangles 3}' and 'player: 236 samples, 1 ..., worst p99.9 8.67, 472 problem lines {470, 2}' (captures/review/done_when.log).

**Unratcheted extremes** (captures/review/full_suite.log:3753-3789):

- hero x37.23 (getup_front peak), flex spine twist x27.07.

skeptic.reason: The core claim holds. At 3eea29a the `problems_max` assertion in A7 can never fail for either shipped art. The title "cannot fail" is overstated, because two other ratchets stay live. NaN and floor lines are asserted to be 0 on the lines just above, so a run that produces them already fails. The ceiling is therefore 2N+6. I derived N as (46 ANIM_IDS + 3 Punk moves) x 5 phases + 6 flexes = 251, and 46 x 5 + 6 = 236 for the hero. This matches the logged sample counts. Both caps are above their ceilings, so neither could ever have fired. (3) Nothing else in the suite holds p0.1, max, min or the per-sample p99.9. test_art_punk's A19 test only asserts no NaN, no floor and more than 200 samples. test_motion_m4's deformation ratchet runs on the primitive placeholder body, not the GLBs. The Punk-only 10 cm visible-stretch ratchet (8.4 cm today) is a partial extra guard, and the hero has none. (4) What does guard A7 is the single worst p99.9 and the flex-triangle share. The p99.9 caps are 4.6 against 4.12 and 9.5 against 8.67. The flex share is 2% against the Punk's 1.62% and the hero's 0.63%, so the hero can grow about 3x. These cannot see a few mis-weighted vertices: a vertex touches roughly 6 edges, p99.9 sits at roughly the 20th-worst edge, and the Punk's flex margin is 54 triangles. findings.evidence:

Crops: captures/review/probe/c2_tape_4x.png (C2 f109, the wraps), probe/c1_mouth_4x.png and probe/c1_cap_4x.png (C1 f109), sheets/v1_J2J4_cap_mouth_tape_laces.png.

Threshold the mask in toon.gdshader so lines are hard at any magnification and the faint values drop out:
`float r = texture(detail_tex, UV2).r; float w = max(fwidth(r), 1e-4); float a = smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, r); color = mix(color, ink, a * detail_strength);`
This applies to the player's mask too: re-check F-player's lines at 0.3-0.6 m. Then re-check test_art_contract's face-ink and tape tests and C1/C2/C8 crops. Optionally bake the Punk's mask at 2048 (punk.json detail_bake.size) for thinner lines.

The Punk's interior ink lines (tape wraps, mouth, nose) render as feathered, dotted grey strokes at 1 m, because the shader blends the bilinear-filtered 1k mask into the albedo with no threshold. This is a real defect against J4 (critical, "crisp interior lines") and J2 (face "crisp"). No call, spec line or approved departure covers it. - C2 f109 tape wraps: solid, crisp ink strokes, no feathering or grey specks.
- C1 f109 mouth: a crisp dark bar. The nose scratch is now one clean short stroke, and the faint smudges around it are gone.
- Player: I recorded 'Look: own limbs' before and after (f115 fist at 0.3-0.6 m). The player's lines stay and are slightly crisper, with no loss of readability.
- tools/run_tests.sh -gselect=test_toon.gd: 34/34 pass with the patch. Its string asserts ('texture(detail_tex, UV2).r', 'color = mix(color, ink,') still match. test_art_contract's face-ink test reads the mask PNG, not the render, so the shader change cannot affect it.

Side effects of the threshold, which are not reasons to refute:
- Lines get bolder and blacker, for example the mouth.
- Where the mask itself is broken, a gap shows more plainly, for example one tape-wrap gap near the centre.
- Faint 0.1-0.5 segments drop out. The player's mask is 33% faint texels, so some faint hairlines there vanish. I judged that crisper rather than worse.

skeptic.root_cause: game/fx/toon.gdshader line 67 does color = mix(color, ink, texture(detail_tex, UV2).r * detail_strength). The sampler is filter_linear_mipmap and the value is used raw, with no cut-off. The mask is baked by tools/pipeline/pipe_detail.py as soft, 1-texel-wide lines: a smoothstep of ink_low..ink_high on the black top-hat, resampled bilinearly onto a 1024 UV2 atlas. At 1 m one mask texel covers about 1.5-2 screen px. Bilinear magnification then feathers every line into a grey gradient, and the faint tail (0.1-0.5) draws as grey speckle. Hard lines at any magnification need a threshold at sample time, with an fwidth-based smoothstep for anti-aliasing.
